impact.note: Seeing cost is the precondition for judging value per dollar.
impact.consider: Attributing cost to outcomes is what makes Cost per Accepted Output computable; without attribution, value per dollar has no denominator.

impact.note: No strong direct interaction.
No strong direct interaction.
Visibility reveals where routing, caching, or batching would pay off.
impact.consider: Where cost and latency concentrate tells routing, caching, and batching where to act first.

impact.note: Attribution and budgets are what governance controls act on.
impact.consider: Attribution and trends are the signals budgets and chargeback/showback policies enforce.

impact.note: Value gives cost its meaning.
impact.consider: Value gives cost its denominator; the same spend reads differently once divided by trusted outcomes.

impact.note: Acceptance data is the gate that makes prompt cuts safe.
impact.consider: Acceptance data is the quality gate (Quality-Gated Cost Reduction) that lets you compress prompts without shipping a regression.

impact.note: Utilization and acceptance tell you what context to trim.
impact.consider: Utilization and acceptance tell you what context to trim; trim by utilization, never a flat cap.

impact.note: Value and risk signals decide when to escalate vs route cheaper.
impact.consider: Value and risk signals drive Cost-to-Value Escalation: spend more only where the outcome warrants it.

impact.note: Outcome evidence is what governance decisions rest on.
impact.consider: Outcome evidence is what quality gates and governance sign-offs rest on.

impact.note: Fewer input tokens directly lower cost.
impact.consider: Fewer input tokens and a cacheable stable prefix cut cost directly.

impact.note: Over-compression drops what kept answers correct.
impact.consider: Compress past clarity and you drop the instruction or example that kept answers correct. Gate every prompt cut on acceptance (Principle 3).

impact.note: No strong direct interaction.
Smaller, stable prompts cache and route more cheaply.
impact.consider: A stable, compressed prefix caches and routes more cheaply.

impact.note: No strong direct interaction.
Less context sent means lower cost and latency.
impact.consider: Less context sent is lower input cost and latency.

impact.note: Trim past utilization and grounding collapses.
impact.consider: Trim past what the answer uses and grounding collapses; measure utilization first and let grounding gate the trim (RAG Right-Sizing).

impact.note: No strong direct interaction.
Less context is cheaper and faster to execute.
impact.consider: A smaller context window is cheaper and faster to execute.

impact.note: Careless trimming can bypass access and freshness rules.
impact.consider: Careless pruning can drop access-aware selection or serve stale sources; context governance must survive the trim.

impact.note: Routing, caching, and cascades lower spend.
impact.consider: Routing, cascades, and caching lower spend per call.

impact.note: A cheaper model or stale cache can drop acceptance.
impact.consider: A cheaper model or a stale semantic-cache hit can drop acceptance; gate cascades and cache reuse on quality (Semantic Cache with Trust Gate).

impact.note: No strong direct interaction.
No strong direct interaction.
Routing, caching, and local models create policy risk.
impact.consider: Routing, caching, and local models create data-handling and policy risk; route sensitive data by tier and gate cache reuse.

impact.note: Budgets and policies bring spend under control.
impact.consider: Budgets and policies bring spend under control and keep it there.

impact.note: Quality gates protect accepted outcomes.
impact.consider: Quality gates protect accepted outcomes from unchecked cost cuts.

impact.note: No strong direct interaction.
Governance enforces source trust, access, and freshness.
impact.consider: Governance enforces source trust, access, and freshness on retrieval.

impact.note: Controls add friction and latency to execution.
impact.consider: Controls and approvals add friction to routing and experimentation; scale the control to the risk tier (Governance-by-Risk Tier), not uniformly.
